newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LAWTON, MOLITOR POWER TWINS PAST TIGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LAWTON, MOLITOR POWER TWINS PAST TIGERS.

text.p: Matt Lawton hit a three-run homer and Paul Molitor had a grand slam in a seven-run second inning to help the Minnesota Twins to their best start in 10 years.

The Twins beat the Detroit Tigers 10-6 on Thursday to sweep their season-opening three-game series for Minnesota's best start since beginning with four wins in 1987, the year they won the World Series.

Todd Ritchie earned the win in his major-league debut, allowing a run and three hits with three strikeouts over three innings. Dan Naulty, the third pitcher used by Minnesota in the ninth, retired Brian Hunter on a groundout with runners on first and second for his first save.
Willie Blair lasted just 1 2/3 innings, allowing seven runs and four hits with three walks for Detroit.
Molitor big blast was just his third career grand slam, his last coming against Minnesota in 1994 when he was playing for Toronto.
"As indicated by the numbers it's not something I have done very frequently," Molitor said. "Being able to hit a grand slam like that, who knows maybe it's the comet."
In Anaheim, Jason Dickson threw his first career complete game, a five-hit shutout in just his eighth major-league start, as the Angels blanked the Boston Red Sox 2-0.
Dickson allowed just five singles and no Red Sox batter reached second base. He struck out five and walked none, throwing 67 of 100 pitches for strikes.
The Angels scored on an RBI single by Garret Anderson in the seventh and and a sacrifice fly by Jim Edmonds in the eighth.
Boston starter Tim Wakefield allowed two runs and six hits in 7 1/3 innings, walking two and striking out one.
In Oakland, Geronimo Berroa's solo home run to deep left field with one out in the eighth inning lifted the Athletics to a 5-4 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
Eric Plunk, who gave up Berroa's homer took the loss. Richie Lewis worked the eighth inning to earn his first win as an Athletic.
Kevin Mitchell belted a three-run homer for Cleveland in the second. Mark McGwire had a solo shot off Indians starter Orel Hershiiser in the fifth.
Marquis Grissom, acquired by Cleveland in the blockbuster pre-season tade with Atlanta, got his first hit as an Indian and stole two bases.
In Baltimore, Rafael Palmeiro homered and Chris Hoiles had a two-run single as the Orioles rallied for three runs in the eighth inning to beat the Kansas City Royals 6-4.
Arthur Rhodes picked up the win by pitching two scoreless innings of relief. Royals closer Jeff Montgomery came on to open the eighth and suffered the loss.
Jay Bell went 3-for-4 for the Royals with a two-run homer in the fifth that gave Kansas City a 4-2 lead.
